topics.title: Aristotle's fallacy and the law of inertia

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why Aristotle's view that a force is needed to keep a body moving uniformly is wrong.
Interpret Galileo's inclined-plane experiments that led to the law of inertia.
Define inertia as the resistance of a body to a change in its state of rest or uniform motion.
State Newton's first law and relate zero net external force to zero acceleration.
Explain everyday and space situations using Newton's first law.

topics.title: Newton's second law of motion and impulse

concepts.learning_objective: Apply F = dp/dt = ma to calculate forces and accelerations, including apparent weight.
Relate impulse to change in momentum and explain how stretching the impact time reduces force.
Identify action-reaction pairs and recognise that they act on different bodies.
Calculate the mutual contact force between bodies accelerated together.
State the law of conservation of momentum for an isolated system.
Apply momentum conservation to recoil, explosions and sticking collisions.
Apply the condition that the vector sum of concurrent forces is zero for equilibrium.
Resolve forces into components to find unknown tensions in equilibrium.
Explain the self-adjusting nature of static friction and the limiting value mu_s N.
Compare kinetic, static and rolling friction and use the angle of repose.

topics.title: Circular motion and solving problems in mechanics

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the force supplying centripetal force for vehicles on level and banked roads.
Use free-body diagrams to solve connected-body and circular-motion problems.
